h: פָּרָשַׁת אַחֲרֵי מוֹת, י״א Acharei Mos, 11
Nighttime Preparation and Daytime Honor Complete the Shabbos Meals

p: "The honor of the day and the honor of the night:
the honor of the day takes precedence."
"And therefore one must set the table
even on the day of Shabbos as well";
implying that the main thing is the night meal
(and the Magen Avraham already raised this,
בְּמָגֵן אַבְרָהָם סִימָן רעא, סְעִיף קָטָן ד)
are the words of the living God,"
and one master said one thing
and the other master said another,
For certainly from the side of the person
the main preparation is at night,
for then is the meal of the Field of Apples,
from the side of Knesses Yisrael;
and at night comes the mitzvah
"Remember the day of Shabbos to sanctify it":
"remember it over wine at its entry,"
as they said in the Gemara (there, Pesachim 106a).
And so the mitzvah then "to sanctify it,"
as it says (Midrash Rabbah, beginning of Parshas Eikev,
and the main thing is at night,
for then the meal is that of the Field of Apples.
And about this the holy Zohar says
"even on the day of Shabbos as well";
for by day the meal is that of Atika,
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
"to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you";
also set the meal on it.
And nevertheless the Gemara rightly said
that if he has something choice
with which to delight the Shabbos,
"the honor of the day takes precedence":
for then the meal is that of Atika,
and he must honor the day
and the honor of the meal of Atika;
brings in the holiness from His side.
for then is the time for work,
and Hashem Yisbarach has satisfaction from this,
"that He spoke and His will was done";
is like the eating of offerings,
"that He spoke and His will was done"

Honoring the Holiness Bestowed by Day

paragraphs.text: Source: Pesachim 106a — “הכי קאמר: ״זכור את יום השבת לקדשו״ — זוכרהו על היין בכניסתו, אין לי אלא בלילה, ביום מנין? תלמוד לומר: ״זכור את יום השבת״.” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 223) — “The Gemara answers that this is what the tanna is saying: “Remember the day of Shabbat to sanctify it” is a mitzva to remember it over wine when it begins. I have only derived the obligation to recite kiddush at …”

paragraphs.text: Source: Shemos 20:8 — “זכור את יום השבת לקדשו” — “Remember the sabbath day and keep it holy.”

paragraphs.text: Source of the quoted words: Pesachim 105a — “איתיביה: כבוד יום וכבוד לילה כבוד יום קודם. ואם אין לו אלא כוס אחד — אומר עליו” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 221) — “Ravina raised an objection to the opinion of Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak from another source: If there is a choice between the honor of the day of Shabbat and the honor of the night, the honor of the day takes …”
